story: A debut that started behind Alonso into Turn 1 and finished ahead of him. Third place, first time out.
First pole, first win, sixth start. A race interrupted by four safety cars and led from lights to flag.
Fifth was the number that mattered. It arrived at Turn 13 of lap 71, and it arrived by one position and one point.
Won by 68 seconds in standing water. The largest winning margin of the V8 era at Silverstone.
A hydraulic failure in qualifying, fourteenth on the grid, and rain arriving at the point in the race when Vettel led. Won it.
A single set of intermediates run for fifty laps on a resurfaced, saturated circuit. Seventh title, by thirty-one seconds.
Disqualified from qualifying, five-place engine penalty, twentieth in the sprint. Won the Grand Prix from tenth.
Led 57 of 58 laps. The championship was decided on the last of them, after a safety car restart, on a set of tyres 40 laps older than the car behind.
A ninth win at Silverstone and a first anywhere in 945 days, in a race that rained twice and needed three tyre calls to be right.
Sprint pole and a sprint win in the third weekend in red. The Grand Prix result did not follow, and neither did a podium for the rest of the season.
The 106th Grand Prix victory, the first for Ferrari, from second on the grid across 66 laps.
